agrees_with_project_vocabulary.claim: the join covers the two relations a content can be asked about; the other three are reported as unstateable, never guessed

honest_limits: The answer rate is 1.0 and that number alone means little: the control shows some doors are matched by every candidate. `mv`'s move was matched by 59 of 59 candidates, so the join's answer there carries no information; `rm`'s move was matched by 3 of 47, which does. Both are reported per program, and the coverage is part of the result.

Only 5 distinct moves were found among 62 rows. The vocabulary is coarse: it says whether a move adds, removes, renames, rewrites or destroys, not what it did with the bytes. Two doors that both 'rewrite' are one move to this join.
A goal about MEANING (is this a valid PNG, is the text French, is the archive intact) is not expressible and is refused by name. That is a real limit of the five relations.

The census's door set varies between identical runs on git: measured 42, 40 and 42 doors across three runs of the same code. This is pre-existing in round 3, not introduced here, and it is why the fleet total for git is reported as a range.
Producer-run sandbox only. No independent identity re-ran any of it; truth.achieved stays false.

leave_one_out.note: a refusal means no OTHER door made that move; it is the honest limit of predicting a move from a single run, not an error

the_unit.door_is: the move it was measured to make, on the same relations
the_unit.goal_is: a demanded move of one or more relations
the_unit.join_is: the door must move every relation the goal demands, same direction
the_unit.saved_row_contains: no path, no argv, no content, no example

the_one_invented_relation.name: LOT
the_one_invented_relation.why: the project's five relations are commutative -- they are functions of a SET of pairs -- so `mv a b` and `rm a` were indistinguishable: both remove a name. LOT is a function of the STEP, not of a state: was every readable content still readable afterwards? It separates retention from destruction and needs no new observable, only the order of the two states the project already recorded.

unstateable_goal.why: the five relations are functions of the attested structure; a goal about what the bytes MEAN is not a function of that structure, so no door can be matched to it by this join

what_was_wrong_first.second_design: the project's five relations, as a signature per door
what_was_wrong_first.third_design: the five relations plus LOT, a function of the step not of a state
what_was_wrong_first.why: all five relations are commutative -- functions of a SET of pairs -- so a rename and a delete of one file were identical, and MUCH of the surface collapsed into one class
